Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciated the practical examples you shared about patient intake workflows. Per our call, you had a few specific asks on how Redwood handles PII in prompts and model outputs, where logs are stored, and retention policies. Below is a quick recap and the items we promised to confirm: 

1) What is stored by default (prompts/outputs)?
- Short answer: hosted API request and response payloads (full prompt and output text) are logged for debugging and observability by default. More details coming from our security team.

2) Where data is stored / residency options
- Hosted: logs and artifacts are stored in region-specific S3 buckets (we support us-east and eu-west in hosted today).
- Dedicated/Private: data can remain in your VPC or on-prem and not leave your network.

3) Retention and access controls
- Default retention windows and options (we'll confirm exact numbers with security).

Next steps I propose: 1) Our security lead (Mina) will confirm retention windows and whether logs are used for model training; 2) We can run a brief tech deep-dive to review logging / KMS; 3) I'll send the PII handling summary and a sample retention table.

Attaching the summary and retention table now. If you need a signed SOC 2 report, we can share under NDA.

Hi Sara — Mina from Security/Compliance here. Quick answers and the matrix you requested below. Happy to join a 30–45m tech/security deep-dive next week.

Summary (high level) — Hosted API default behavior
- What is stored: by default, Redwood's hosted API stores request and response payloads (full prompt + model output) in encrypted object storage for observability, billing, and debugging. We also retain request metadata (timestamps, model variant, token counts) for billing and monitoring.
- Training: Redwood DOES NOT use customer prompts/outputs from the Hosted tenant logs to train public models. We have a strict policy and controls; customer content is segregated and only used for debugging/ops unless an explicit opt-in agreement is signed.
- Retention: default retention for full payload logs is 30 days for hosted customers. Billing/usage aggregates (no raw text) are retained for 12 months by default.
- Access controls: logs are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and SSE-KMS; access is RBAC-restricted and audited. We can furnish audit logs for access on request.

Private / Dedicated options (for PHI/regulated workloads)
- Dedicated: logs can be stored in a customer-dedicated storage account/namespace; retention policy is configurable by the customer (can be shortened to 0 days for full payloads).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): request/response logs never leave the customer's environment unless configured to forward; Redwood control plane can be isolated and operate under your KMS.

PII-specific controls and redaction options
- Client-side redaction: recommended approach — customers can preprocess prompts to remove or tokenize PHI before sending.
- Ingest-side masking: we offer templated PII redaction at the API gateway (names, SSNs, MRNs) — this removes sensitive fields before logs are persisted.
- Hashing/Tokenization: we can hash specific user identifiers so that the model sees a consistent identifier but raw values are not stored.

Short matrix (what / where / retention / notes):
- Full request payloads (prompt + output): Hosted: US region default; retention 30 days; stored encrypted; not used for training. Dedicated/Private: customer-configurable, can be 0 days.
- Billing & token metrics: Hosted: retained 12 months (aggregated, no raw text); Dedicated: retained per contract.
- Audit/Access logs: retained 12 months by default; can extend on request.
- KV cache / runtime state: ephemeral; not persisted beyond session unless customer opts-in.

Compliance and evidence
- We are SOC 2 Type II certified; we share the report under NDA. We also provide a security questionnaire template and canned answers for common vendor assessments.

Attachments included: redwood-pii-handling-2026Q1.pdf (detailing the above, examples of redaction rules) and token-retention-table.csv (sample retention windows).

If desirable, we can prepare a short statement/appendix tailored to Acme Health's PHI requirements and your legal team's template. Proposed next step: tech deep-dive (security + infra) — please share two 1-hour slots and we'll confirm.

— Mina
